metaDescription: Instant guitar chord diagrams for any chord name — Cmaj7, Am7, D/F♯ and more. Open-position fingering for 100+ chords. Free web app and Chrome extension.
h2Decoder: How to decode a chord name
decoderIntro: Any chord symbol is built as: Root + quality + extensions + /optional bass. This table covers 95% of what you'll find in guitar tabs online.
rowRoot: C D E F G A B ± #/b
rowDom7: Major triad + minor 7th (♭7). The engine of blues and jazz.
rowHalfDim: Minor with lowered 5th + ♭7. Typical ii° chord.
rowSus: The 3rd is replaced by the 2nd or 4th (open sound, no major/minor color)
rowAdd: Adds the indicated note without a 7th.
rowSlash: Play the chord but put X in the bass.
callout: Diagram convention: you're looking at the neck face-on. The thinnest string (high E, 1st) is on the right; the thickest (low E, 6th) is on the left. Numbers above indicate the finger (1=index, 2=middle, 3=ring, 4=pinky). ○ = open string, ✕ = muted string.

dimPageTitle: Diminished chords on guitar · Guitar Chords
dimMetaDescription: The 12 diminished chords (dim7) on guitar, with the movable fingering on the 6th, 5th and 4th string. Ready-to-play diagrams for any position on the neck.
dimLead: The diminished seventh chord (dim7) is symmetric: moving it three frets repeats the same notes, in a different order.
dimLeadForms: It has three shapes, depending on which string carries the lowest root: the 6th, 5th, or 4th string.
dimSection6Lead: The lowest shape: the root sounds on the 6th string (low E), with the 5th and 1st strings muted.
dimSection5Lead: Same idea, one string up: the root sounds on the 5th string (A), with the 6th and 4th strings muted.
dimSection4Lead: The most compact shape: only two frets wide, with the root on the 4th string (D) and the 6th and 5th strings muted.

tabPageTitle: Free Online Guitar Tab Maker · ASCII Tab Editor
tabMetaDescription: Free online guitar tab editor: type fret numbers on all six strings, drag notes around and copy the tab as plain ASCII text to paste anywhere.
tabHowTo1: Click (or tap, on a phone) the string and beat where the note goes.
tabHowTo2: Type the fret number: 0 is the open string and you can go up to fret 24.
tabHowTo3: Keep going with <kbd>Enter</kbd> or the arrow keys. A new line appears when you reach the end; to move a note, drag it.
tabHowTo4: When you're done, hit the copy button and paste the tab into a message, a document or a forum.
tabKeyDigits: Types the fret at the highlighted spot.
tabKeyNext: Go to the next beat (with Shift, the previous one).
tabWhat1: A tablature (or tab) shows which fret to press on each guitar string. Each line is a string: the 1st (high E) on top and the 6th (low E) at the bottom. Numbers are frets, read from left to right. It's called ASCII because it uses only text characters, so it looks the same anywhere.
tabWhat2: The example above is a C major arpeggio: 3rd fret on the 5th string, 2nd on the 4th, open 3rd, 1st fret on the 2nd and open 1st, and back down.
tabRead1: The lines are strings, not staff lines: the top one is the highest string.
tabRead2: A 0 means open string; any other number is the fret to press.
tabRead3: Numbers stacked in the same column sound together (a chord); one after another, they're played in order.
tabFaq1A: Yes, in your browser. Come back to this page on the same device and they'll be just as you left them. Nothing is uploaded to a server.
tabFaq2Q: Does it work on my phone?
tabFaq2A: Yes. Tapping a string opens the number pad, and the lines wrap to fit the screen width.
tabFaq3Q: Where can I paste the tab?
tabFaq3A: Anywhere that takes text: a chat, an email, a document or a guitar forum. Use a monospaced font so the columns line up.
tabTutorialSummary: How to use the editor: drag, duplicate and fill with zeros
tabTutorialIntro: The keys highlighted in colour are the ones to press.
tabDragBody:
Click a note, drag it to another string or beat and drop it.
If you drag from an empty spot you select several notes and move them together.
tabDupBody: With the cursor on a beat, press <kbd>Alt</kbd> (or <kbd>⌘</kbd> on a Mac) together with <kbd>→</kbd> to copy its notes to the next beat.
tabZeroBody: For chords with open strings, press <kbd>Alt</kbd> (or <kbd>⌘</kbd>) together with <kbd>0</kbd> and the empty strings of the beat are filled with 0.

privMetaDescription: What data acordesdeguitarra.com.ar collects: Google Analytics, files uploaded to Score to tab, IP addresses for usage limits and Cloudflare Turnstile.
privLead: This site is free and has no user accounts. Here is what data is collected and what happens to it.

p: We use Google Analytics to learn which pages are visited and to improve the site. Google may store cookies and browsing data under its own policy. We do not use that data to identify you.
If you use the Score to tab tool, your file (PDF or MusicXML) is stored in private storage, only to process it and produce the results (PDF, MusicXML and JSON).
Your job link contains a long random identifier that works as a secret: anyone with the link can see the result. All files, original and generated, are deleted automatically after 24 hours.
Your edits in the editor are also kept in your browser (local storage) so they survive a reload; you can remove them by clearing the site data.
To prevent abuse we store your IP address along with a daily count of jobs created. These records are deleted automatically and are not used for anything else.

To check that a person is creating a job, we use Cloudflare Turnstile, which loads only on the Score to tab page. Turnstile may receive technical data from your browser under Cloudflare's privacy policy.

Upload only scores you have the right to use. You are responsible for the content you upload. If you are a rights holder and want a work removed, write to hola@acordesdeguitarra.com.ar with the job link.

Under Argentina's Personal Data Protection Law 25.326 you may access, correct and delete your personal data. The Agency for Access to Public Information is the supervisory body for this law. To exercise your rights, write to hola@acordesdeguitarra.com.ar.

partMetaDescription: Upload a PDF or MusicXML score and get the same sheet music with guitar tablature added under every measure. Automatic fingering, a tab editor and downloads as PDF, MusicXML and JSON.
partLead: Upload a PDF or MusicXML score and we give it back as it is, with the guitar tab added under every measure.
partExampleCaption: When you upload the PDF, the tab is added below the staff.
partExampleAlt: Measures 6 to 9 of a guitar score with their tab in standard tuning. Numbers indicate frets; 0 means an open string.
partHowH2: How tab is added to your sheet music
partHow1Body: A PDF or a MusicXML file. For a PDF we recognize the notation first.
partHow2Body: Each note is placed on the most comfortable string and fret of the guitar, in standard tuning or Drop D. Then you can edit the tab to correct it as you see fit.
partHow3Body: See it under every measure, fix the tab in the editor and download it as PDF, MusicXML or JSON.
partFaq1Q: What is tablature and how is it different from sheet music?
partFaq1A: Sheet music says which note to play and for how long. Tablature says which string and fret of the guitar to play it on. Here the sheet music is kept and the tab is added below it.
partFaq2A: Scores as PDF or MusicXML (.mxl, .musicxml, .xml). MusicXML gives the most accurate result because the notation does not need to be recognized.
partFaq3Q: Is it free? Do I need an account?
partFaq3A: It is free and needs no sign-up. Only upload scores you have the right to use.
partFaq4A: Yes. The tab can be edited measure by measure and downloaded together with the score.
